stem_book: In the equation a sin x + b cos x = c, when is there no solution? (a) If a = 0 and b = 0 (b) If c > √(a² + b²) (c) If c < √(a² + b²) (d) Both B and C
reason: key d vs working b: (c) c < √(a²+b²) includes e.g. c = 0, which always has solutions, so 'Both B and C' is false; key d only holds if (c) meant c < −√(a²+b²), which is not what is printed.
work: solvable ⇔ |c| ≤ √(a²+b²); c > √(a²+b²) ⇒ no solution; c = 0 < √(a²+b²) ⇒ tan x = −b/a solvable
